Gloves make hand hygiene unnecessary when they are changed between patients.

Compassion fatigue is a sudden reaction to one especially bad call.
High compassion fatigue scores simply mean the clinicians chose the wrong profession.
Only new, inexperienced clinicians are at risk of losing compassion for patients.
questions.explanation: Compassion fatigue is the gradual lessening of compassion over time with sustained caregiving.

questions.explanation: His detachment and cynicism, exhaustion, and declining work quality all grew out of chronic job stress, matching burnout rather than a single bad call.

Patients should be told the illness is most likely a common cold virus and does not need follow-up.

Abrasions should be left uncovered so they can dry out during the shift.

Gloves alone are enough protection even when the EMT has open cuts on the hands.

choices: Mask the suspected TB patient, wear a fit-tested respirator yourself, and notify the receiving hospital and public health authorities.
Wear gloves and a surgical mask, since drug-resistant TB spreads by contact with skin and surfaces.
Isolate only after a laboratory confirms drug resistance, which can take several weeks.
Open the vehicle windows and skip respirators, because moving air eliminates the airborne risk.

Hold the formal group session in the open bay anyway, since it is the only part of the program that matters.

Use insect repellent, cover exposed skin where practical, and check themselves for ticks and bites after outdoor calls.

Avoid all skin contact with patients outdoors, since the disease passes by touch.

Hold one debriefing the night of the call and consider the stress response finished once it is held.
Wait at least a month before offering any debriefing so responders have time to process on their own.
Make debriefing available only to responders who ask for it, since most recover without it.

questions.question: After a gunman killed 23 people at a cafeteria in Killeen, Texas, in 1991, the EMS workers who responded were offered a critical incident stress debriefing within 24 hours and were checked again 8 to 10 days later and at 1 month. Suppress the arousal completely before starting, because any arousal during testing lowers scores.
Ignore the sensation and hope it passes, because mindset about arousal has no measurable effect.

Wait to see whether the patient tests positive before reporting anything.
Finish the transport, then mention the exposure at the end of the shift if symptoms develop.
